title: Nutrition in Plants
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: A leaf of a bean or hibiscus plant, a leaf peel under the microscope for stomata, and the starch test on a leaf done by the teacher (boiling in water and spirit are teacher-only steps). A plant kept in the dark for two days beside one in light is the investigation.

skills.key_step: The child names the external parts of a leaf (blade, midrib, veins, petiole) and the internal ones (upper epidermis, palisade layer with many chloroplasts, spongy layer with air spaces, stomata) and says how each suits photosynthesis.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the parts of a plant cell.
floor.question: Which part of a plant cell makes food?

representations: a leaf peel under a microscope
steps: Broad, thin blade: catches light, short path for gases.
Palisade layer near the top: many chloroplasts.
Spongy layer: air spaces for gases.
Stomata: let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out; veins carry water and food.

board.do: Draw a leaf cross-section with layers.
Point at the tightly packed top layer.
board.say: Why does this layer have the most chloroplasts?

board.do: Wait for "it gets the most light".
Ask the child to mark the stomata.

misconceptions.ask: What did we see on the leaf peel?
misconceptions.repair: Stomata let gases in and out.

misconceptions.ask: Which parts of the plant are green?

listen_for: a narrow leaf catches more light
misconceptions.ask: Which catches more light: a broad leaf or a narrow one?
Where did the coloured water go?

checks.question: Why are most chloroplasts in the palisade layer?
checks.answer: it is near the top surface and gets the most light

checks.question: What is the job of the stomata?
checks.answer: let gases in and out of the leaf

skills.key_step: The child describes photosynthesis (carbon dioxide + water gives glucose + oxygen, using light and chlorophyll), the conditions it needs, and the starch test with iodine that shows it happened.

floor.prerequisite: Knows carbon dioxide is a gas in air that plants use.
floor.question: Which gas do plants use to make food?

representations: a plant in light and one in the dark
steps: Raw materials: carbon dioxide and water.
Products: glucose (stored as starch) and oxygen.
contexts: a water plant giving off bubbles

board.do: Write "light and chlorophyll" over the arrow.

misconceptions.ask: Which gas goes into the leaf in the equation?
What are the bubbles from the water plant?
Did the soil weigh much less after the plant grew?
misconceptions.repair: Plants make food in their leaves.

checks.question: Name the two raw materials of photosynthesis.
A leaf covered with foil for two days gives no blue-black colour with iodine. Why?
checks.answer: no light reached it, so no starch was made
